issues.failure_explanation: The remark after Theorem th:reduction_SVcones_anglescones asserts that sigma is a (P,Q)-singular value of A iff arccos(sigma) is a critical angle between the lifted cones. The theorem's proof shows critical values scale by ||A||: the critical value of MA(P~,Q~) corresponding to sigma is sigma/||A||, so the critical angle is arccos(sigma/||A||), not arccos(sigma). As written the claim is false whenever ||A|| != 1; e.g., A = 2I, P = Q = R^n has singular value sigma = 2, for which arccos(sigma) is undefined (the correct critical angle is arccos(1) = 0).

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, $\sigma$ is a $(P,Q)$-singular value of $A$ if and only if $\arccos(\sigma)$ is a critical angle between $\wt P$ and $\wt Q$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace arccos(sigma) by arccos(sigma/||A||) (or explicitly assume ||A|| = 1 in the remark).
issues.overall_effect: Only this unlabeled remark is false as written; the correct correspondence (with sigma/||A||) is what is actually used elsewhere, e.g., in Corollary cor:saddle_ConeSV, so no labelled result is invalidated.
issues.title: Remark misstates the singular value / critical angle correspondence (missing division by \|A\|)
issues.why_classification: minor_issue: local correction of a standalone remark with no dependents; the true correspondence is already the one used by the rest of the paper, so no claim, method, or guarantee changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $-\Vert A\Vert\leq \langle u,Av\rangle\leq\Vert A\Vert$ for all feasible pair $(u,v)$ of $\SV(A,P,Q)$

issues.failure_explanation: The text claims that the case lambda* = ||A|| (the optimal value of SV(A,P,Q) equals ||A||) is equivalent to P and Q having a single generator with G^T AH a nonnegative 1x1 matrix. Since |<u,Av>| <= ||A|| on the whole feasible set, lambda* = ||A|| forces <g_i,Ah_j> = ||A|| for every i,j, i.e., Ah_j = ||A||g_i, which forces all g_i to coincide and all h_j to coincide with g^T A h = ||A|| - strictly stronger than mere nonnegativity of the 1x1 matrix. The stated criterion has false positives: with A = I_2, P = R_+ e_1, Q = R_+ e_2 both cones have one generator and G^T AH = (0) is nonnegative, yet lambda* = 0, not 1 = ||A||. Hence the asserted equivalence is false as written (the forward direction alone only yields G^T AH = (||A||)).

failure_location.quote: However, the case $\langle u, Av\rangle =    \|A\|$ is easy to check, since it is equivalent to say that both $P,Q$ have only one generator and $G^\top AH$ is a $1\times 1$ nonnegative matrix.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claimed equivalence by the correct criterion: lambda* = ||A|| iff P = R_+ g and Q = R_+ h are single rays with g^T A h = ||A|| (still checkable in polynomial time), or delete the sentence.
issues.overall_effect: A standalone false characterization of the boundary case lambda* = ||A||. No labelled result or algorithm relies on it: Algorithm alg:active_set requires G^T AH not >= 0, which already implies lambda* < ||A||, and the preprocessing handles lambda* >= 0 directly, so the error does not propagate.
issues.title: False equivalence claimed for the boundary case lambda* = \|A\|
issues.why_classification: minor_issue: one-sentence correction with no dependents; the advertised polynomial-time verifiability of this case survives under the corrected criterion, and no theorem, algorithm, or guarantee changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
$\lambda:= - \sqrt{\rho(A_yA_x)}$ is the least eigenvalue of $ M:= \begin{pmatrix}
       0& A_x\\A_y& 0  \end{pmatrix}$,
the spectral radius of $A_yA_x$ is $\rho(A_yA_x) = \|U_G^\top AU_H\|^2$

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses allow rho(A_yA_x) = ||U_G^T A U_H||^2 = 0 (e.g., \bar G = [e_1], \bar H = [e_2], A = I, both full column rank). Then item 2 gives lambda = 0, so the matrix (A_x U/lambda; U) whose image defines V is undefined, and the proof's computations dividing by lambda break down; items 3-4 are then ill-defined. The proposition needs the extra hypothesis rho(A_yA_x) > 0 (equivalently lambda != 0).

failure_location.quote:
let $V$ be an orthogonal basis for the image of  $ \begin{pmatrix}
      A_xU/\lambda\\ U  \end{pmatrix}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis rho(A_yA_x) > 0 (equivalently lambda != 0) to the proposition; optionally remark that the degenerate case rho = 0 (least eigenvalue 0) can never improve the negative incumbent in Algorithm alg:active_set.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition's construction of V and its items 3-4 are undefined in the degenerate case rho(A_yA_x) = 0, so the result is ill-defined as stated. Its only application, Algorithm alg:active_set, invokes it only after the test rho(A_lambda) > lambda^2 with an incumbent lambda that is always negative (initial lambda = min entry of G^T AH < 0 under the algorithm's requirements), hence with rho > 0; no algorithm or other labelled result is affected.
issues.title: Proposition pro:sufficient_conditions_feasibility misses the hypothesis rho(A_yA_x) > 0 (division by lambda = 0)
issues.why_classification: minor_issue: the repair is adding a standard local nondegeneracy condition; the proposition's content and its guarded algorithmic use are unchanged and no claim or guarantee is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: then compute $a = \sqrt{2n}x = [a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{\lceil(n-1)/2\rceil}]$ and $\lambda = \sqrt 2 y = [\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \dots, \lambda_{\lceil(n-1)/2\rceil}]$

issues.failure_explanation: With the substitution as written, x = a/sqrt(2n) and y = lambda/sqrt(2), the constraints of the previous line (||a||^2 = 1/(2n), ||lambda||^2 = 1/2) give ||x||^2 = 1/(4n^2) and ||y||^2 = 1/4, not ||x|| = ||y|| = 1 as the next displayed line claims, and the objective becomes 8 sqrt(n) sum x_k y_j cos(2 pi jk/n), not (2/sqrt(n)) sum x_k y_j cos as displayed: the equality between the second and third lines of the computation is false as written. The correct substitution is x = sqrt(2n) a, y = sqrt(2) lambda, which makes the whole chain and the final matrix M correct. The same inversion is inherited by the recovery sentence after the lemma ('a = sqrt(2n) x, lambda = sqrt(2) y' instead of a = x/sqrt(2n), lambda = y/sqrt(2)); it is harmless there only because the angle objective is invariant under positive scaling of a and lambda.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Swap the substitution in the proof to x = sqrt(2n) a, y = sqrt(2) lambda (then ||x|| = ||y|| = 1 and the objective coefficient 2/sqrt(n) both follow), and change the recovery sentence to a = x/sqrt(2n), lambda = y/sqrt(2) (or note that the pair is only needed up to positive scaling).
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma lem:equivalence_circulant_SPN_SNN contains a false displayed equality as written, and the post-lemma recovery formulas are inverted; the lemma's statement (equivalence of MA(CP_n, CN_n) with PSV(M) for the stated M) is nevertheless correct, so the circulant-cone experiments that rely on it are unaffected.
issues.title: Wrong change of variables in the proof of Lemma lem:equivalence_circulant_SPN_SNN
issues.why_classification: minor_issue: a local correction of the change of variables and of the scale-insensitive recovery sentence; the lemma's statement, the matrix M, and all downstream computations are unchanged, and no new nontrivial argument is required.
